sections.title: Crop rotation and soil-borne pests: UC IPM home and landscape guidance
sections.text: Reviewed summary of UC IPM guidance for home and landscape plantings. Rotation changes the plant grown in a location to interrupt pest and disease cycles. Repeatedly planting susceptible crops in the same soil can maintain pest populations. Rotation choices should consider botanical families because related crops can share pests. The appropriate rotation depends on the pest, host range and persistence in soil. This general guidance does not specify a validated commercial-field rotation for every crop or disease. Ask for the previous crops and known disease history before suggesting a sequence.
